paragraphs.title: The Restoration and Expansion of Israel

easy.explanation: The verse addresses the barren woman as a picture of Israel.
easy.q: To whom is the command “Sing, O barren” addressed?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent.”
easy.q: What is the woman told to enlarge?

easy.explanation: The children of Israel will make the desolate cities inhabited.
easy.q: What will happen to the desolate cities?

medium.explanation: She is told to rejoice because she will have more children.
medium.q: Why is the barren woman told to sing and cry aloud?

answers: Lengthen the cords and strengthen the stakes
medium.explanation: The verse commands, “lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.”
medium.q: What must be done after stretching out the curtains?

medium.explanation: A desolate city is empty, ruined, or forsaken.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “desolate” mean?

answers: Because her household will greatly increase
Because she is leaving the land
Because the cities will be destroyed
challenge.explanation: The coming increase of her children requires more room.
challenge.q: Why does the woman need to enlarge her tent?

challenge.explanation: The passage pictures Israel changing from a barren condition to abundant growth.
challenge.q: What change is pictured by the movement from barrenness to many children?

answers: To the right and to the left
challenge.explanation: The KJV says, “thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left.”
challenge.q: In which directions will Israel spread?

paragraphs.title: The Renewal of the Relationship Between the Lord and Israel

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed.”
easy.q: What is Israel told not to fear?

answers: Maker, husband, Redeemer, and the God of the whole earth
easy.explanation: The Lord is called Israel’s Maker, husband, Redeemer, and the God of the whole earth.
easy.q: Which description is given to the Lord in verse 5?

easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “with great mercies will I gather thee.”
easy.q: What will the Lord do after briefly forsaking Israel?

answers: The shame of her youth and the reproach of her widowhood
medium.explanation: She will no longer remember the shame of her youth or the reproach of her widowhood.

answers: The Lord temporarily withdrew His favor
The Lord called Israel to battle
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a temporary withdrawal before the promise of everlasting kindness.
medium.q: What does “I hid my face from thee” mean in this context?

answers: The forsaking is brief, while the gathering is merciful and abundant
They last exactly the same length of time
medium.explanation: The brief forsaking is contrasted with gathering through great mercies.
medium.q: How are the small moment of forsaking and the great mercies of gathering related?

answers: His promise is firm and dependable
challenge.explanation: The Lord compares His promise to His oath that the waters of Noah would not again cover the earth.
challenge.q: What does the reference to the waters of Noah teach about the Lord’s promise?

answers: His kindness is more permanent than things that may be removed
The mountains are the source of His kindness
challenge.explanation: Even if the mountains depart, the Lord’s kindness and covenant of peace will remain.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by comparing the mountains and hills with the Lord’s kindness?

answers: From forsaking and hiddenness to mercy and a covenant of peace
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from temporary anger and hiddenness to everlasting kindness and peace.
challenge.q: What change in the relationship between the Lord and Israel is described?

paragraphs.title: The Rebuilding of Zion and the Renewal of Her Children

answers: Afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted
easy.explanation: The verse addresses the afflicted woman who has been tossed by the tempest and not comforted.
easy.q: How is Israel described at the beginning of verse 11?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions sapphires and other precious stones.
easy.q: What will be used in the foundations of the restored city?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.”

medium.explanation: The verse declares, “great shall be the peace of thy children.”
medium.q: What will result from the children being taught of the Lord?

medium.explanation: Oppression is unjust treatment or the abuse of power.
medium.q: What does “oppression” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The passage says she will be far from oppression and that terror will not come near her.
medium.q: From what must Israel remain far away so that she will not fear?

challenge.explanation: The costly materials portray a restored and glorious dwelling.
challenge.q: What do the precious stones used in the rebuilding symbolize?

answers: A righteous society can live securely without fear
They remove the need for teaching
challenge.explanation: Being established in righteousness is linked with distance from oppression and terror.
challenge.q: How are righteousness, safety, and freedom from oppression connected?

answers: A movement from distress to a stable and renewed society
A movement from peace to fear
A movement from rebuilding to destruction
challenge.explanation: The verses describe comfort, rebuilding, instruction, peace, and righteous stability.
challenge.q: What progression is shown from comfort to establishment in righteousness?

paragraphs.title: Divine Protection from Enemies and Destructive Forces

answers: He will fall for Israel’s sake
easy.explanation: The verse says, “whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall for thy sake.”
easy.q: What will happen to anyone who gathers against Israel?

answers: It will become a precious stone
easy.explanation: The KJV declares, “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.”
easy.q: What will happen to every weapon formed against Israel?

easy.explanation: Their heritage is connected with the failure of weapons and with righteousness from the Lord.
easy.q: What is the heritage of the servants of the Lord?

answers: He created both the maker and the destroyer
He has no authority over the destroyer
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I have created the smith” and “I have created the waster to destroy.”
medium.q: What does the Lord say about the smith and the destroyer?

answers: One who destroys or lays waste
medium.explanation: A waster is a destructive person or force.
The verse mentions weapons and every tongue rising against Israel in judgment.
medium.q: What two forms of attack are mentioned in verse 17?

answers: The Lord controls both the forces that create and those that destroy
The destroyer is stronger than the Lord
challenge.explanation: The Lord identifies Himself as the Creator of both the smith and the waster.
challenge.q: What central idea is shared by verses 15 and 16?

answers: Protection includes defense from accusations as well as physical attacks
It explains how the children are taught
It describes the building of the city
challenge.explanation: The promise covers both violent weapons and hostile accusations.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention a tongue rising in judgment as well as weapons?

answers: Protection and righteousness are the promised portion of the Lord’s servants
They will receive only desolate cities
challenge.explanation: The closing verse identifies protection from attacks and righteousness from the Lord as their heritage.
challenge.q: What does “the heritage of the servants of the Lord” mean here?
